interpretation: The proof reaches randomized zeta through an ordered approximation pipeline: shifted two-point kernels first provide second-moment control and negative-Sobolev tightness; actual zeta is then approximated by a fixed finite Euler product, that fixed shifted truncation converges in law to the independent-phase randomized truncation, and only afterward is the truncation removed to obtain an almost-sure generalized-function boundary value.

The finite truncation gains a comparable bridge between vertical shifts and independent phases, but loses the full Euler product; the comparison therefore requires T to tend to infinity at fixed N before N is removed.

Smoothness of the total error requires both mechanisms to satisfy their own summability conditions.

This yields an L2-bounded negative-Sobolev martingale with a nontrivial generalized-function limit.

After a logarithmic change of variables, log randomized zeta is a Brownian spectral field plus a smooth additive error.
